instruction: Using Visual Studio Code, create a Python script named `goodreads_top100_rating_analysis.py` in the `/home/user/analysis_results/goodreads_books/` directory. In this script: (1) navigate to `https://www.goodreads.com/list/show/1.Best_Books_Ever` and scrape the top 100 books from that page, extracting for each: `title`, `author`, `average_rating`, and `review_count`. (2) Create a scatter-plot of `average_rating` (y-axis) vs `review_count` (x-axis), fit a simple linear regression line, and save the plot as `rating_vs_reviews.png` in the same directory. (3) Compute the correlation coefficient between review count and average rating, and decide whether books with higher review counts tend to have higher ratings. Save a CSV file named `goodreads_top100_summary.csv` with columns: `title`, `author`, `average_rating`, `review_count`. Also save a text file named `goodreads_correlation_summary.txt` containing exactly one line formatted as: `Corr_ReviewCount_Rating: <value>, Trend: <Increases/Decreases/None>` indicating if the trend is positive (Increases), negative (Decreases) or no clear trend (None).
